scenario_prompt: Write only the opening paragraph of an executive summary, addressed to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer. The opening paragraph must restate the buyer's own situation, in the buyer's own terms, before naming any vendor, product, or capability. Context: the buyer is spending $1,850,000 a year running an on-premises Microsoft SQL Server and Hyper-V estate, and its next compliance audit opens in 6 months. Return only that one opening paragraph.
text:
**Artifact family:** an executive summary.

No customer source material (RFP text, discovery notes, stated requirements) was supplied for this task. Please provide it if it exists. Without it, the `PF-3.3` provenance override cannot fire, and every term below is judged by the deletion test alone.

---

You spend $1,850,000 a year to run your on-premises SQL Server and Hyper-V estate. Your next compliance audit opens in six months. That run-rate buys you capacity you already own and already maintain, and it does not shrink in the months before the auditors arrive [PF-2.4 GAP: the split of the $1.85M between licensing, hardware refresh, and staff time was not supplied, so the share the audit puts at risk cannot be stated]. You are funding both at once: the estate as it stands today, and the evidence work the audit will ask for [PF-2.4 GAP: the audit's scope, framework, and control set were not supplied, so the evidence burden cannot be described]. This document proposes a shift — from an estate you pay to keep audit-ready to one where that evidence is produced as a by-product of running it.

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| GAP: cost breakdown of the $1.85M run-rate | PF-2.4 | The buyer's split of the figure across licensing, hardware, and staff time |
| GAP: audit scope and control set | PF-2.4 | The framework and controls the six-month audit covers |
| GAP: no baselined metric in the opening | PF-2.13 | A measure with a buyer-stated baseline and its source — the $1.85M has no stated provenance (PF-1.14) |
| GAP: no differentiator present | PF-2.13 | An evidenced statement of vendor capability; none can be written before a vendor is named |
| REVIEW (compliance): "audit-ready" and the by-product claim | PF-2.17 | Confirmation that the proposed approach actually satisfies this buyer's named control set |

The before/after contrast and the opening reframe are present. The remaining additive-sweep items — baseline and differentiator — are marked above rather than invented.
